I've been playing PnP RPGs for a couple of years now. One of my favorite things that my GM uses a fair amount is his yes/no die. Anything that can be boiled down to a 50/50 question when a decision can't be made is left to the dice gods. Recently I've started GM'ing my own game of Pathfinder and I wanted to be able to replicate this fun and unique die. At first I was simply written "yes" and "no" on the sides of a blank die, but that was pretty cheesy. It lacked the quality of a professional die. So I threw my blank in the mill at my work and engraved the sides. Here's an album of the finished result: http://imgur.com/a/ZsDNu

Bonus: Here's the hand made leather dice bag that the person playing the Druid in my campaign made for me: https://i.imgur.com/LTYS39M.jpg
I thought I'd share one of my proudest hobby accomplishments, my custom made Yes/No die!

The reason the 3DS succeeded where the Vita fell short was that Nintendo put their full support behind the 3DS, while Sony rarely gave the Vita more than a token effort.

Looking back at the 3DS's first year, just in 2011, it's fascinating how much top tier support they gave the handheld. Games like Nintendogs + cats, Super Mario 3D Land, and Mario Kart 7 were made by Nintendo's EAD studios, the same ones responsible for the console equivalents of the same series. The same Kyoto studio that made the Super Mario Galaxy duo, two of the best rated games of all time, was tasked with making a major release tailored for the 3DS. Sure, not every Nintendo game for the 3DS was top tier (Steel Diver), but it was clear that Nintendo was pouring their best efforts into it.

Sony released games from acclaimed series for the Vita, but it was hardly the same thing. Uncharted: Golden Abyss wasn't made by Naughty Dog, it was made by Bend Studio. Naughty Dog had been too busy making Uncharted 3 and The Last of Us for the PS3. The Vita version of ModNation Racers was not made by United Front, since they were busy working on LittleBigPlanet Karting for the PS3. Resistance: Burning Skies was not made by Insomniac, because they were too busy making a new Ratchett & Clank for the PS3. See the pattern?

Nintendo may have some dry spells, but support their hardware. Even the Wii U is still getting big games despite poor hardware sales.
